findings.summary: Tenant history detail opens for users lacking the detail endpoint permission
findings.details: `TenantTransactionHistoryPage` grants row drill-in when the user has either `action.redemption.view_history` or `action.redemption.view_all_history`, then mounts `TransactionDetailSheet`, which calls `GET /redemption/requests/{id}`. The local contract still marks that detail endpoint with `x-permission: action.redemption.view_history`, and the repo's permission pattern explicitly says page-level `view_all_history` must not imply detail access. A client admin with only `view_all_history` can therefore click tenant rows and hit an unauthorized detail request, producing a broken admin workflow and noisy forbidden calls.
findings.recommendation: Gate row click and sheet mounting on `can("action.redemption.view_history")` only, or update the backend contract and implementation to explicitly allow `view_all_history` before enabling that UI path.
findings.note: This is the canAny(view_history, view_all_history) code committed per the user decision (detail accessible via EITHER permission). The FE is committed AHEAD of the required BE/contract change, so until GET /redemption/requests/{id} accepts view_all_history this is a live bug window for view_all_history-only admins. Decision pending: ship FE+BE together, or revert FE gate to view_history-only until BE lands.

findings.summary: Tenant-wide export is triggered without the ALL_TENANT scope
findings.details: The tenant admin history page renders `ExportDialog` with only `filters`, while `ExportDialog` forwards its `scope` prop into the export POST body. Personal and company history pass explicit `PERSONAL` and `COMPANY` scopes, but tenant history leaves it undefined. Since the export job model says scope determines which records are included at generation time, this can silently export the wrong dataset or fail depending on backend defaults. The E2E named `CLIENT_ADMIN exports tenant-wide data` only stubs any `/export` POST and never asserts the request body includes `ALL_TENANT`, so this regression is not caught.
findings.recommendation: Pass `scope="ALL_TENANT"` from `TenantTransactionHistoryPage` and add unit/E2E coverage that inspects the export POST payload, including tenant filters such as `userId` and `companyId`.
findings.note: VERIFIED: <ExportDialog .. filters={exportFilters}/> at line 378 passes no scope prop; ExportDialog.scope is optional and forwarded into the export POST body; personal/company tabs pass PERSONAL/COMPANY. Pre-existing in redemption-history (NOT introduced by reward-balance-expiration or by my permission fix).

findings.summary: Redemption-only users fall through the root redirect to an unauthorized profile route
findings.details: The branch adds a `/redemption-store` route protected by `module.redemption_store`, but `HomeRedirect` still only considers home, activity review, incentives, rewards, and profile permissions before falling back to `/settings/profile`. A user whose only module is the new redemption store can authenticate successfully but be redirected away from their only allowed module, likely into a protected profile route they do not have permission for.
findings.recommendation: Add `{ permission: "module.redemption_store", path: "/redemption-store" }` to `HOME_ROUTES` and cover a `module.redemption_store`-only user in the redirect tests.
findings.note: VERIFIED: HOME_ROUTES lacks module.redemption_store and the fallback is /settings/profile (a protected route). Matches the documented CLAUDE.md HomeRedirect maintenance rule. Pre-existing (module.redemption_store predates this branch).

adversarial-review.codexOutput:
# Codex Adversarial Review

Target: branch diff against main
Verdict: needs-attention

No-ship: tenant history still has permission-contract and export-scope failures that can break admin workflows, plus the new redemption module is not reachable from the root redirect for redemption-only users.

Findings:
- [high] Tenant history detail opens for users lacking the detail endpoint permission (src/pages/redemption-history/TenantTransactionHistoryPage.tsx:201-210)
  `TenantTransactionHistoryPage` grants row drill-in when the user has either `action.redemption.view_history` or `action.redemption.view_all_history`, then mounts `TransactionDetailSheet`, which calls `GET /redemption/requests/{id}`. The local contract still marks that detail endpoint with `x-permission: action.redemption.view_history`, and the repo's permission pattern explicitly says page-level `view_all_history` must not imply detail access. A client admin with only `view_all_history` can therefore click tenant rows and hit an unauthorized detail request, producing a broken admin workflow and noisy forbidden calls.
  Recommendation: Gate row click and sheet mounting on `can("action.redemption.view_history")` only, or update the backend contract and implementation to explicitly allow `view_all_history` before enabling that UI path.
- [high] Tenant-wide export is triggered without the ALL_TENANT scope (src/pages/redemption-history/TenantTransactionHistoryPage.tsx:375-379)
  The tenant admin history page renders `ExportDialog` with only `filters`, while `ExportDialog` forwards its `scope` prop into the export POST body. Personal and company history pass explicit `PERSONAL` and `COMPANY` scopes, but tenant history leaves it undefined. Since the export job model says scope determines which records are included at generation time, this can silently export the wrong dataset or fail depending on backend defaults. The E2E named `CLIENT_ADMIN exports tenant-wide data` only stubs any `/export` POST and never asserts the request body includes `ALL_TENANT`, so this regression is not caught.
  Recommendation: Pass `scope="ALL_TENANT"` from `TenantTransactionHistoryPage` and add unit/E2E coverage that inspects the export POST payload, including tenant filters such as `userId` and `companyId`.
- [medium] Redemption-only users fall through the root redirect to an unauthorized profile route (src/components/HomeRedirect.tsx:5-11)
  The branch adds a `/redemption-store` route protected by `module.redemption_store`, but `HomeRedirect` still only considers home, activity review, incentives, rewards, and profile permissions before falling back to `/settings/profile`. A user whose only module is the new redemption store can authenticate successfully but be redirected away from their only allowed module, likely into a protected profile route they do not have permission for.
  Recommendation: Add `{ permission: "module.redemption_store", path: "/redemption-store" }` to `HOME_ROUTES` and cover a `module.redemption_store`-only user in the redirect tests.

Next steps:
- Fix the permission gate and tenant export scope before shipping.
- Add request-body assertions for tenant export and root redirect coverage for redemption-only roles.
